clues: This city in Russia sits where two rivers join. It lies northwest of Moscow, the capital city, a trip of a few hours.
Winters here are long, snowy and cold, yet the hardest frosts are rare. Summers turn warm and humid, with heat that climbs high.
This city went by a changed name from nineteen thirty one to nineteen ninety. Then it took its old name back.
Three rivers meet here and split the town into halves and quarters. Water cuts the place into pieces like a puzzle.
Its White Trinity Church was built in fifteen sixty four of pale stone, not brick. No other building here is left from that early age.
